Dukes legislation to establish responsible AI policies for schools advances through House Education Committee
Rep. Brandon Dukes
October 6, 2026 | 9:50 AM
HARRISBURG, Oct. 6 –
Today, legislation sponsored by state Rep. Brandon Dukes (H.B. 2786) to establish responsible artificial intelligence policies for schools advanced through the PA House of Representatives Education Committee.
The bill would require Pennsylvania schools to adopt a clear local policy governing the responsible use of AI by students and staff, including acceptable and prohibited uses, required human oversight of AI-generated content, and data transparency for students and families.
“With artificial intelligence use becoming more prevalent outside of the classroom, now is the time to set clear definitions and policies in our schools,” Dukes said. “Without these policies, every school in the commonwealth will be subject to questions of academic integrity, student privacy and transparency. I urge my House colleagues to take up this legislation and curb this uncertainty around AI use in our classrooms.”
House Bill 2786 will now head to the full House for consideration.
More information on the bill is available at:
https://www.palegis.us/legislation/bills/2025/hb2786
.

Dukes, Harris to hold grant information session in Butler County
Rep. Brandon Dukes
October 2, 2026 | 10:47 AM
CRANBERRY TOWNSHIP, Oct. 2 –
On Thursday, Oct. 8, state Rep. Brandon Dukes and House Appropriations Chairman Rep. Jordan Harris will host an informative session about Pennsylvania state grant opportunities.
The event will be held from 6 p.m. to 8 p.m.. at the
Cranberry Township Municipal Center, 2525 Rochester Road
. Dukes and Harris will be joined by state agencies to dispense valuable tips on grant funding resources, application best practices, and how to find the right grant program for an organization. There will also be a question-and-answer period.
“There are many wonderful grant funding initiatives in the commonwealth that officials and organizations may not know about,” Dukes said. “That’s why I’m pleased to put this event together alongside Chairman Harris, so we can get Butler County better informed and connected to programs that can provide much-needed assistance.”
“Too often, organizations doing important work miss out on state funding because they don’t know what’s available or how to navigate the application process,” Harris added. “Rep. Dukes and I want to help change that. This grant seminar will put Butler County organizations in the room with the people who can explain the opportunities, answer their questions and help them take the next step.”
Media coverage is invited.

Dukes secures $1.3 million for nine Butler County projects
Rep. Brandon Dukes
September 15, 2026 | 12:23 PM
BUTLER COUNTY, Sept. 15 –
Today, state Rep. Brandon Dukes announced that $1.3 million in funding from the Department of Community & Economic Development’s Local Share Account will go toward projects in Butler County.
A total of nine projects will benefit from the allotment, which is provided by the distribution of gaming revenues through the Commonwealth Financing Authority.
The LSA allotment will go toward the following:
$500,000 for storm sewer installation in Zelienople Borough.
$250,000 to support the eventual construction of a recreation center in Cranberry Township.
$100,000 for stormwater improvements in Mars Borough.
$100,000 to modernize the current EMS building in Jackson Township.
$100,000 for the purchase and upfitting of a plow truck in Harmony Borough.
$100,000 to make improvements in EDCO Park in Evans City Borough.
$50,000 for storm sewer system upgrades in Evans City Borough.
$50,000 for the construction of a salt shed, maintenance garage and storage yard in Evans City Borough.
$50,000 for the replacement of a culvert in Evans City Borough.
“Quality infrastructure is the backbone of quality life in Butler County,” Dukes said. “It keeps us safe in times of crisis, empowers our first responders and supports a strong community. I’m proud to secure funding that helps our infrastructure keep up with our rapidly growing district.”
For more on the LSA program, visit:
https://dced.pa.gov/programs/local-share-account-lsa-statewide/
.

Dukes, Venkat introduce inheritance tax reform legislation for family-owned businesses
Rep. Brandon Dukes
September 10, 2026 | 3:23 PM
HARRISBURG, Sept. 10 –
This week, state Reps. Brandon Dukes, D-Butler, and Arvind Venkat, D-Allegheny, introduced legislation that would modernize the family business and family agricultural asset exemption to the state’s inheritance tax.
The legislation (
H.B. 2769
) would reduce the amount of time a family business or family agricultural business must have been in the same family to qualify for an inheritance tax exemption from 7 years to 5 years. The legislation would also increase the maximum amount of assets a qualified family-owned business may have to qualify for an inheritance tax exemption from $5 million to $6.9 million.
Dukes, the prime sponsor of the bill, said that the proposal preserves family businesses while granting much-needed flexibility.
“I know firsthand how much my district relies on the efforts of family-owned establishments, and I want to help them sustain for generations to come,” Dukes said. “That’s why I took on this issue as my first piece of legislation in the House. Every family business has crucial ties to its community, and we need to provide the proper access and resources for these bonds to remain strong.”
Venkat, the co-prime sponsor, echoed that the legislation would fortify the relationship family establishments have with communities in the state.
“Every family business in Pennsylvania has a different story, whether it be a new startup or a staple of the community for generations,” Venkat said. “This legislation will ensure that more family businesses can qualify for inheritance tax exemptions so these establishments can stay where they belong – in our communities and in the family. I look forward to collaborating with Representative Dukes on this legislation that will support the family-owned businesses that keep regions like the North Hills and Cranberry moving.”
An informational hearing of the House Finance Committee on the legislation will take place at a future date
.
For more information on the bill, visit
https://www.palegis.us/legislation/bills/2025/hb2769
.

Dukes takes oath of office to serve Pennsylvania's 12th Legislative District
Rep. Brandon Dukes
September 8, 2026 | 2:58 PM
HARRISBURG, Sept. 8 –
Today, state Rep. Brandon Dukes was sworn in to serve as state representative for Pennsylvania’s 12th Legislative District, located in Butler County.
Dukes was elected to office when he won a special election on Aug. 18, becoming the first Democrat to represent the district in decades.
“I am so grateful to serve this district that I call home,” Dukes said. “I look forward to providing my fellow residents with crucial state government services and advocating for their needs here in Harrisburg. I’d also like to thank my fellow House lawmakers, who have welcomed me with open arms as we work toward a better commonwealth.”
A graduate of the University of Pittsburgh, Dukes spent 16 years working in the financial industry prior to his election. He currently lives in Cranberry Township with his wife and daughter. Dukes said his key issues include modernizing infrastructure, prioritizing affordability and investing more resources in educational institutions such as community colleges and trade schools.
“We are happy to welcome newly-elected Representative Brandon Dukes as the 103rd member of the House Democratic Caucus,” Speaker of the House Joanna McClinton, D-Phila/Delaware, said. “Our caucus has kept its promise to put working families, seniors and students first since securing the majority nearly four years ago. We’ve cut taxes for seniors, families and small businesses and delivered record funding to our public schools, while bringing compassion, stability, and common sense to governing at a time when our neighbors are reeling from the chaos in Washington. Now, Representative Dukes’ voice will be added to those who are advocating for more affordable, safer and more equitable communities.”
The 12th District consists of the townships of Cranberry, Adams and Jackson; as well as the boroughs of Callery, Evans City, Harmony, Mars, Seven Fields, Valencia and Zelienople.
Residents can visit Dukes’ Cranberry Township office at 2525 Rochester Road, or his office can be reached by phone at 724-824-8671. His Harrisburg office can be reached at 717-783-4303.

PA Treasury could be holding your unclaimed property
Rep. Brandon Dukes
August 19, 2026 | 4:37 PM
Each year, the Pennsylvania Treasury receives millions of dollars of unclaimed property. It is estimated that roughly one in 10 Pennsylvanians has unclaimed property.
Unclaimed property may include:
Closed bank accounts
Uncashed checks, including paychecks
Lost stocks and bonds
Contents of safe deposit boxes
Proceeds from the demutualization of insurance companies
Expired gift cards/gift certificates
To find out if you have unclaimed property, search your name in the Unclaimed Property database at
https://www.patreasury.gov/unclaimed-property/
or call 1-800-222-2046. There is NO CHARGE to claim your unclaimed property.

Dukes secures PennDOT commitment to fund majority cost to finish Route 228 improvement project
$102 million needed to complete construction of project’s final phase
Rep. Brandon Dukes
October 14, 2026 | 7:17 PM
CRANBERRY TOWNSHIP, Oct. 14
– The redevelopment of Route 228 in Butler County is nearing its final stages after decades of construction, but there are hurdles that still need to be cleared before the last portion of construction can begin. During a House Majority Policy roundtable discussion on the future of Route 228 and the final phase of construction, hosted by Rep. Brandon Dukes (D-Butler), Pennsylvania Dept. of Transportation (PennDOT) Secretary Mike Carroll announced PennDOT has committed to funding more than half of the remaining cost of the $102 million needed to complete the project.
“The whole project has been in the works for decades. There are people who have lived in this community their entire lives who have never seen it fully completed. Route 228 serves as a main artery for Cranberry Township and Butler County as a whole, with millions of drivers using it every year,” Dukes said. “Widening and improving this corridor is vital to easing congestion and improving the commute for the people who live, work, and travel here.”
Route 228 Corridor Improvement Projects underway at PennDOT are aimed at updating the safety and efficiency of the route from Route 8 to Route 19. The “Mars Railroad West Project” addresses the last remaining section needed to fully tie the completed Route 228 corridor together. The work extends from Franklin Road to just west of Pittsburgh Street, and includes intersection upgrades and roadway widening through Seven Fields Borough and Adams and Cranberry Townships.
"Route 228 is a critical corridor for Butler County and as the region grows, so does the need to complete the final section, tying all the improvements together," said PennDOT Secretary Mike Carroll.
"PennDOT is committed to doing what we can to advance this effort, and I'm grateful to Rep. Dukes for convening this important discussion.”
While the final portion of the project is currently funded for all pre-construction phases, approximately $102 million dollars is needed for actual construction of this final phase. During the hearing, Sec. Carroll committed PennDOT to funding more than half of the money needed to complete this project. Butler County recently applied for a federal infrastructure grant for $50 million. If that grant application is approved at a significant amount, PennDOT will fund the remainder of the project cost.
“I’m extremely grateful to Secretary Carroll and his team for committing to funding the remainder of the project if Butler County receives a federal infrastructure grant. I also want to thank the important decision-makers in our community for all the work they’ve done on this project to get us where we are today,” Dukes said. “With the committed funding from the state, we’re one step closer to finally finishing this important project.”
“We have reasons to be optimistic about this project, but the optimism must be matched with action,” said House Majority Policy Chairman Ryan Bizzarro (D-Erie). “We need our partners at the federal level to get off their hands and help us secure this money. We owe it to the people of Butler County to ensure the progress that’s already been made translates into meaningful improvements for the drivers who depend on this road every day.”
In addition to PennDOT Secretary Mike Carroll and PennDOT District 10 Executives Brian Allen and Alice Hammond, members were joined by all three
Butler County Commissioners
and representatives from
Cranberry Township
,
Seven Fields Borough
, the
Butler County Planning Commission
, and the
Southwestern Pennsylvania Commission
.

Dukes: Over $100,000 in tax credits awarded to support Butler County programs
Rep. Brandon Dukes
October 22, 2026 | 10:52 AM
CRANBERRY TOWNSHIP, Oct. 22 –
Today, Rep. Brandon Dukes announced that $107,250 in Neighborhood Assistance Program investments will go toward community revitalization projects in his district.
Inspired Hearts and Hands, Inc., located in Cranberry Township, received $74,750 in NAP investments to provide approximately 1,917 additional food distributions to economically disadvantaged households throughout Butler County. Another $32,500 will go toward Nonprofit Development Corporation to provide no-cost critical repairs to income-constrained older adult homeowners in Butler County, making homes safer and more accessible.
NAP provides tax credits to businesses that contribute to nonprofit organizations’ efforts to revitalize communities. Businesses can receive tax credits of up to 95% on contributions they make to a qualifying community project. Categories of projects under NAP include affordable housing programs, community services, crime prevention, education, job training and neighborhood assistance.
“I’d like to thank the commonwealth for supporting our local fight against food insecurity and supporting safer homes in our communities,” Dukes said. “We’re making the necessary investments to ensure no resident of Butler County goes without food or without an accessible roof over their head.”
For more information on NAP, visit:
https://dced.pa.gov/programs/neighborhood-assistance-program-nap/
.
